summary: Explains `any_errors_fatal`, set at play or block level: on an error, Ansible finishes the failing task on the current batch then stops the play on all hosts, skipping later tasks and plays, and a rescue can recover. Example ensures every load balancer is disabled before upgrading frontends.
questions: How do I stop everything if any host fails a task?
Can I set any_errors_fatal on just a block?
Does any_errors_fatal stop the following plays too?
Can a rescue section recover from any_errors_fatal?
How do I make sure all load balancers are disabled before stopping the service?

answer_card.title: Abort on first error with any_errors_fatal
answer_card.answer_md:
With `any_errors_fatal`, when a task errors Ansible finishes that task on all hosts in the current batch, then stops the play on **all** hosts; later tasks and plays don't run. A `rescue` section can recover. Set it on a play or a block:

```yaml
- hosts: somehosts
  any_errors_fatal: true
  roles:
    - myrole

- hosts: somehosts
  tasks:
    - block:
        - include_tasks: mytasks.yml
      any_errors_fatal: true
```
Use it when everything must succeed to continue, e.g. put `any_errors_fatal: true` on the play that disables load balancers so frontends are only upgraded if every load balancer was disabled.
